Splitter.purpose: Splits one bus into several narrower buses, or joins several into one. Each output fan carries a bit range.
Splitter.usage: `fanout` = how many branches, `incoming` = the input bus width, and each `bit<i>` names the bit index that branch starts at (LSB-first numbering).
Splitter.traps: Bit ranges are LSB-indexed from the INPUT side; a range that runs past `incoming` silently drops bits. Fan-out wires are at (loc.x+20, loc.y-10-10*(fanout-i)), 20 px apart.
Splitter.behaviour_source_reachability: derived from the local source path; not verified

Transistor.purpose: A single MOS transistor acting as a voltage-controlled switch between its INPUT and OUTPUT, controlled by the GATE.
Transistor.usage: `type` selects n or p. Ports are named INPUT, OUTPUT and GATE in the source (Transistor.java:52-54), and `type` and `facing` MOVE them: INPUT is at (40*dx, 40*dy) and GATE at (20*(dx+dy), 20*(-dx+dy)) for n-type, with different signs for p-type.
Transistor.traps: The ports are NOT called source/drain - they are INPUT, OUTPUT and GATE, and their coordinates change with `type` and `facing`, so a hard-coded offset only works for one configuration. An open transistor leaves its OUTPUT floating, which reads undefined unless something pulls it.
Transistor.behaviour_source_reachability: derived from the local source path; not verified

Transmission Gate.purpose: A bidirectional switch: connects its two terminals when the control pair is asserted.
Transmission Gate.usage: Needs both a control and its complement to open and close.
Transmission Gate.traps: Bidirectional - do not use it where direction matters; it will pass a value either way.
Transmission Gate.behaviour_source_reachability: derived from the local source path; not verified

Tunnel.purpose: Connects two points by LABEL rather than by geometry - the only connection mechanism this skill emits.
Tunnel.usage: Put a Tunnel exactly ON each port that shares a net and give them all the same `label`. `width` must match the net's real width.
Tunnel.traps: `width` DEFAULTS TO 1, so a multi-bit net through a width-less Tunnel is silently truncated to bit 0 - measured: a 2-bit AND read `UU` on every row. Two Tunnels at one coordinate are one node, so two different labels there is a short. `facing` is cosmetic (they join by label) but a wrong value draws the glyph over its component: measured, `west` draws to the RIGHT of the port and `east` to the LEFT - the reverse of the names.
Tunnel.behaviour_source_reachability: derived from the local source path; not verified

BitSelector.purpose: Extracts one group of adjacent bits from a bus. `select` chooses which group.
BitSelector.usage: `width` = the input bus width, `group` = how many bits come out. Output = bits [select*group, select*group+group).
BitSelector.traps: The SELECT is multiplied by the GROUP WIDTH to get the shift, so select=1 with group=4 takes bits 4..7. A select past the end of the bus yields the unknown value, not 0.
BitSelector.behaviour_source_reachability: derived from the local source path; not verified

FPSquareRoot.purpose: Square root of a floating-point number.
FPSquareRoot.traps: Two IEEE corners, both MEASURED against the real simulator: sqrt(-0.0) is -0.0, not +0.0; and sqrt of a negative finite value returns a NEGATIVE NaN (0xFC at fpwidth 8), not the canonical positive one. The sign is a PLATFORM behaviour, not Logisim's own - `Math.sqrt` compiles to the x86 SQRTSD instruction, whose default QNaN has its sign bit set, and floatToMiniFloat143 copies that sign into the encoding. On a CPU with a positive default NaN (arm64) the same circuit would produce 0x7C. 121 rows of a conformance case were wrong until this was understood.
